postings.title: [Nyx Earth] Propulsion CFD Engineer
postings.description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building innovative aerospace technologies that advance the future of space transportation.


As a talented Propulsion CFD Engineer, you will be responsible for the computational fluid dynamics analysis of propulsion system components and thruster plumes, providing the flow physics insight that underpins component design, thruster performance, and vehicle-level integration decisions.




ROLE OVERVIEW

 CFD Analysis & Component Simulation

 - Perform CFD simulations of propulsion components — valves, regulators, orifices, injectors, feed lines — to characterize internal flow, pressure drop, and flow-induced loads.

 - Support design trade studies by predicting component-level performance across the operating envelope, in both steady-state and transient conditions.

 - Identify and help resolve flow anomalies such as cavitation, choking, or flow separation that affect component performance.
   

Plume Characterization & Thruster Performance

 - Model thruster plume characterization, from near-field continuum expansion through far-field rarefied flow, including relevant gas dynamics effects.

 - Assess plume-induced thermal, contamination, and force/torque effects on adjacent subsystems and vehicle surfaces.

 - Support thruster and nozzle design by predicting performance parameters such as thrust coefficient and specific impulse from CFD.
   

Cross-Functional Design Collaboration

 - Work closely with propulsion design engineers and structural and thermal analysts to translate CFD results into actionable design inputs and margins.

 - Communicate CFD findings and their implications clearly to multidisciplinary teams and program stakeholders.

 - Support system-level trades on component sizing, thruster placement, and plume shielding for vehicle interfaces.
   

Model Validation, Tools & Documentation

 - Validate and correlate CFD models against test data — cold-flow testing, hot-fire testing, plume diagnostics — to build and maintain model confidence.

 - Maintain and improve CFD simulation workflows, meshing practices, and tools to improve turnaround time and consistency across the design office.

 - Produce clear technical reports and analysis documentation supporting design reviews and certification.





KEY RESPONSIBILITIES



LOCATION

You will perform your duties principally at the Company's premises in Bordeaux and may be required to travel from time to time to our company’s premises in Munich in the course of your duties.



WHAT WE WOULD LOVE TO SEE FROM YOU

 - M.S. or Ph.D. in aerospace or a related field, with 3+ years of hands-on CFD experience relevant to propulsion or fluid dynamics.

 - Proficiency with CFD software such as ANSYS Fluent, STAR-CCM+, OpenFOAM, or equivalent.

 - Experience modeling compressible, multiphase, and/or rarefied gas flows relevant to propulsion valves and thruster plumes.

 - Familiarity with plume characterization methods such as DSMC or continuum-rarefied coupling is a strong plus.

 - Strong grounding in fluid mechanics, thermodynamics, and gas dynamics fundamentals.

 - Experience correlating CFD predictions against test data.

 - Familiarity with scripting or automation (Python, MATLAB) for meshing, post-processing, or workflow automation.

 - Fluent in English. German and French are an asset
   

Skills and Behaviors:

 - A hands-on approach to problem-solving, combined with a collaborative mindset to work across multidisciplinary teams

 - Excellent organizational skills and ability to multitask

 - Capability of working autonomously whilst collaborating productively with remote teams

 - Positive and flexible attitude in a constantly evolving environment

 - Grit to get the job done

 - Ability to communicate effectively with a wide variety of audiences

 - Behaviors consistent with The Exploration Company’s core values of Commitment, Innovation, Trust, Quality, and Teamwork

postings.title: [Nyx Earth] Propulsion Design Office Principal
postings.description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building innovative aerospace technologies that advance the future of space transportation.


Team Leadership & Engineering Management

 - Lead, mentor, and grow a team of engineers spanning thermal, structural/mechanical, CFD and CAD/design functions, fostering a culture of technical excellence and accountability.

 - Define individual scopes of work, set priorities, and manage workload across concurrent design activities to keep the team aligned with program milestones.

 - Conduct regular design reviews and one-on-ones, providing clear technical direction and supporting career development within the office.


Propulsion System Design & Technical Ownership

 - Making or approving key design decisions on feed or pressure systems, and associated structures.

 - Drive design-to-requirements traceability, ensuring system satisfy mass, thermal, and safety margins up to qualification.

 - Coordinate with Systems Engineering and Vehicle Design to manage interfaces between the propulsion system and adjacent vehicle subsystems.


Thermal Analysis & Management

 - Oversee steady-state and transient thermal analyses of propulsion components, ensuring compliance with temperature limits across all mission phases (ground operations, in-orbit, re-entry).

 - Review and approve thermal models, ensuring analytical rigor and correlation with test data.

 - Guide the team in identifying test platforms and defining test objectives.


Structural & Mechanical Design

 - Direct the mechanical design of propulsion structures, and brackets, ensuring adequate strength, stiffness, and fatigue life under load cases.

 - Oversee FEA and hand-analysis efforts to verify structural margins, and lead disposition of any margin concerns or design anomalies.

 - Working closely with AIT team to define and validate integration sequences.


CAD, Documentation & Configuration Control

 - Define and enforce CAD standards, model maturity gates, and drawing release processes within the design office, ensuring consistency and traceability across the propulsion product tree.

 - Oversee the maintenance of the engineering master model and associated bill of materials (BOM), coordinating with PDM/PLM administrators to keep configuration control current.

 - Ensure design documentation — including ICDs, engineering drawings, design notes, and specification trees — is complete, reviewed, and baselined on schedule.

postings.description:

We want you as a highly skilled and experienced AIT Electrical Engineer to help us in our mission by leading the design, commissioning, and debugging of electrical systems for various propulsion test benches, as well as testing of engine electrical systems. This is a dynamic, hands-on engineering position that combines systems-level thinking with practical implementation, demanding both deep technical expertise and the ability to collaborate across multidisciplinary teams.




Key responsibilities:

In your capacity as an AIT Electrical Engineer, your role will be continuously evolving and often diverse, but day to day your duties will include:

 - Contribute to the design and development of electrical systems and architecture for test benches, including power distribution, signal conditioning, and control systems. 

 - Lead assembly, integration and testing of electrical components for turbomachinery and engines.

 - Define test procedures, document results and trace non-conformities

 - Specify and review electrical schematics, panel layouts, and wiring diagrams to ensure system integrity and compliance with industry standards. 

 - Collaborate with the team to integrate sensors, actuators, power supplies, and DAQ systems. 

 - Conduct system-level troubleshooting and debugging, using advanced diagnostic tools (e.g., oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, DMMs). 

 - Perform root cause analysis and implement engineering solutions to improve system robustness and reliability. 

 - Provide technical leadership during assembly, commissioning, and test operations.

 - Document all designs, test results, and configuration changes; contribute to standard operating procedures and risk assessments.

 - Ensure all electrical systems comply with safety and regulatory standards.


Qualifications:

 - Minimum of a Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics, or a related technical field.

What we would love to see from you:

 - Strong understanding of electrical design principles, system integration, and instrumentation.

 - Experience with high voltage systems (200V - 1000V, AC/DC).

 - Comfortable working hands-on with electrical hardware, wiring, test equipment and instrumentation.

 - Proficiency in using common electrical test equipment and CAD tools (e.g., EPLAN, AutoCAD Electrical).

 - Experience with industrial control, automation or data-acquisition systems (e.g. Beckhoff).

postings.title: AIT Thermal/ECLSS Team Leader
postings.description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building innovative aerospace technologies that advance the future of space transportation.


We are seeking an experienced AIT Thermal/ECLSS Team Leader to lead our dynamic AIT thermal/ECLSS team.

In this role, you will be responsible for the planning and execution of thermal/ECLSS integration and testing for Nyx Earth, starting from sub-system level thermal and ECLSS test campaigns. You are requested to lead a small team.

This is a unique opportunity to play a hands-on role in testing and qualifying critical space systems in a fast-paced, innovation-driven environment.

You will report to the AIT Mechanical Principal Engineer.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES:

 - Integration & Test Planning:

Design and plan thermal EVT (environment test) campaign at system/capsule level.

Design and plan all thermal/ECLSS activities at sub-system levels (cold plate qualification, Pressure Compartment System, Ventilation system, etc..) for system and sub-system level.

Support the preparation of engineering drawings for manufacture of test bench components.

Lead team and activities to have a succesful integration of the Thermal system in the Capsule.

 - Hardware Management:

Define and manage flight hardware interfaces during integration (pipes, fittings, valves, MLI, heaters, sensors, harness routing, thermal fillers, etc.).

Design the 3D setup of test activities and build test setup.

Procure test parts and write/execute procedures for all test activities.

 - Test Execution:

Plan, define, prepare, execute, and oversee thermal/ECLSS tests in coordination with internal and external test facilities.

 - Data Analysis & Reporting:

Provide test results and generate comprehensive test reports.

postings.description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building innovative aerospace technologies that advance the future of space transportation.

We are looking for an Avionics Systems Engineer to support the design, development, integration, and validation of spacecraft avionics systems. The role focuses on delivering robust and reliable electronic systems for data handling, communications, and control across all mission phases.

The engineer will contribute to system architecture definition, interface management, verification activities, and requirements engineering, while working closely with multidisciplinary teams and external stakeholders. In this role, you might be assigned to different avionics systems of the spacecraft.

 - Ensure end-to-end consistency of data flows, interfaces, and system-level requirements.

 - Support selection and definition of avionics equipment, computing platforms, sensors, and communication hardware.

 - Contribute to spacecraft-level trade-offs between performance, reliability, mass, power, and cost.


COMMUNICATIONS & DATA HANDLING

 - Define onboard and ground-related communication and data handling concepts.

 - Support implementation of telemetry, telecommand, and data distribution architectures.

 - Ensure reliable data acquisition, processing, storage, and transmission under mission constraints.

postings.title: Building Maintenance Specialist/Fachkraft für Gebäudeinstandhaltung.
postings.description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building innovative aerospace technologies that advance the future of space transportation.

[German version below /Deutsche Version unten]

The Operations team is hiring a hands‑on technician to keep our Munich sites running safely and smoothly. You’ll perform day‑to‑day maintenance, carry out basic repairs, and coordinate certified vendors for the jobs that legally require them. This is a practical, tools‑on role with clear ownership of the site’s essentials.




RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Carry out preventive and corrective maintenance on HVAC (filters/belts/AHUs), plumbing & sanitary hot water, compressed‑air distribution (drains/leaks), lighting and LV electrical basics, doors/gates/roller shutters, and small building works (paint/shelving/furniture).

 - Do weekly visual/functional checks on UPS/central battery/inverters and emergency lighting; raise service tickets when needed.

 - Coordinate statutory inspections with accredited providers (electrical checks, lifts, automatic doors, emergency lighting, sprinklers/fire doors & pumps, smoke extraction) and file the reports.

 - Run water hygiene routines (temperature checks, flushing); book Legionella sampling with the lab and close actions.

 - Support fire safety basics (extinguishers, signage, evacuation routes) and issue/close hot‑work permits for contractors.

 - Look after security systems with the vendor (badges, CCTV, intrusion, alarm teletransmission) and opening/closing routines.

 - Own cleaning, waste & compactor pickups, paper recycling/confidential destruction, and pest/drain services with vendors.

 - Inspect and maintain roof/terrace & gutters (vendor for waterproofing repairs).

 - Oversee landscaping/indoor plants service.

 - If Facilities owns them: coordinate forklifts/MEWPs periodic checks and user daily‑check routines (otherwise interface with Logistics).

 - Use the CMMS/ticketing tool to receive/close work orders, track assets & consumables (filters, softener salt), and report simple monthly KPIs.

 - Act as first response for facilities incidents; make safe and call vendors/EHS as needed.




QUALIFICATIONS / SKILLS

 - 3+ years as a building/facility maintenance technician in industrial, R&D or lab sites.

 - Solid hands‑on skills across HVAC basics, plumbing, and low‑voltage electrical troubleshooting; knows when to fix vs. call a vendor.

 - Comfortable with CMMS and clear, tidy documentation.

 - Can read manuals and simple drawings; uses safe working practices (lockout/tagout basics).

 - German fluent; English workable with vendors and internal teams.

 - Nice to have / or obtained after start: Electrical habilitation (B0/H0 or BS/BE‑manœuvre), SST first‑aid, CACES/authorisations for forklifts/MEWPs; F‑Gas awareness when dealing with HVAC contractors.

Valid driver’s license.


/////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////



Hier bei The Exploration Company entwickeln wir innovative Technologien für die Luft- und Raumfahrt, die die Zukunft des Weltraumtransports vorantreiben.

Das Operations-Team sucht einen praxisorientierten Techniker, der dafür sorgt, dass unsere Standorte in München sicher und reibungslos betrieben werden. Sie übernehmen die tägliche Instandhaltung, führen grundlegende Reparaturen durch und koordinieren zertifizierte Dienstleister für Arbeiten, für die diese gesetzlich vorgeschrieben sind. Es handelt sich um eine praktische Position mit direktem Arbeiten an den Anlagen und klarer Verantwortung für die wesentlichen Bereiche des Standorts.

Verantwortlichkeiten

 - Durchführung der vorbeugenden und korrektiven Instandhaltung von HLK-Anlagen (Filter/Riemen/Lüftungsgeräte), Sanitär- und Warmwasseranlagen, Druckluftverteilung (Abläufe/Leckagen), Beleuchtung und Niederspannungs-Elektroanlagen, Türen/Toren/Rolltoren sowie kleinerer baulicher Arbeiten (Malerarbeiten/Regale/Möbel).

 - Wöchentliche Sicht- und Funktionsprüfungen von USV-Anlagen/Zentralbatterien/Wechselrichtern und Sicherheitsbeleuchtung durchführen; bei Bedarf Service-Tickets erstellen.

 - Gesetzlich vorgeschriebene Prüfungen mit akkreditierten Dienstleistern koordinieren (Elektroprüfungen, Aufzüge, automatische Türen, Sicherheitsbeleuchtung, Sprinkleranlagen/Brandschutztüren und -pumpen, Rauchabzugsanlagen) und die Prüfberichte ablegen.

 - Maßnahmen zur Wasserhygiene durchführen (Temperaturkontrollen, Spülungen); Legionellenbeprobungen beim Labor beauftragen und Maßnahmen nachverfolgen und abschließen.

 - Unterstützung bei grundlegenden Brandschutzmaßnahmen (Feuerlöscher, Beschilderung, Fluchtwege) sowie Ausstellung und Abschluss von Heißarbeitsgenehmigungen für Auftragnehmer.

 - Sicherheitssysteme gemeinsam mit dem Dienstleister betreuen (Zutrittsausweise, CCTV, Einbruchmeldesysteme, Alarmübertragung) sowie Öffnungs- und Schließroutinen durchführen.

 - Verantwortung für Reinigungsleistungen, Abfallentsorgung und Abholung von Müllpressen, Papierrecycling/vertrauliche Aktenvernichtung sowie Schädlings- und Abflussservices durch externe Dienstleister.

 - Dach/Terrasse und Dachrinnen inspizieren und instand halten (Dienstleister für Abdichtungsreparaturen).

 - Pflege der Außenanlagen und Innenpflanzen überwachen.

 - Falls diese in den Verantwortungsbereich von Facilities fallen: Koordination der wiederkehrenden Prüfungen von Gabelstaplern/Hubarbeitsbühnen sowie der täglichen Anwenderkontrollen (andernfalls Schnittstelle zu Logistics).

 - Nutzung des CMMS-/Ticketing-Systems zur Annahme und Schließung von Arbeitsaufträgen, Verwaltung von Anlagen und Verbrauchsmaterialien (Filter, Salz für Wasserenthärtungsanlagen) sowie Erstellung einfacher monatlicher KPIs.

 - Erste Anlaufstelle bei Störungen im Facility-Bereich; Gefahren beseitigen und bei Bedarf Dienstleister/EHS hinzuziehen
   
   Qualifikationen / Fähigkeiten.

 - Mindestens 3 Jahre Berufserfahrung als Gebäude-/Facility-Instandhaltungstechniker an Industrie-, F&E- oder Laborstandorten.

 - Fundierte praktische Kenntnisse in den Bereichen HLK-Grundlagen, Sanitärtechnik und Fehlerbehebung an Niederspannungs-Elektroanlagen; Fähigkeit einzuschätzen, wann eine Reparatur selbst durchgeführt werden kann und wann ein Dienstleister hinzugezogen werden muss.

 - Sicherer Umgang mit CMMS-Systemen sowie strukturierte und sorgfältige Dokumentation.

 - Fähigkeit, Handbücher und einfache technische Zeichnungen zu lesen; sichere Arbeitsweise (Grundkenntnisse zu Lockout/Tagout).

 - Fließende Deutschkenntnisse; ausreichende Englischkenntnisse für die Zusammenarbeit mit Dienstleistern und internen Teams.

 - Von Vorteil bzw. nach Arbeitsbeginn zu erwerben: Elektroqualifikation (B0/H0 oder BS/BE-Manöver), Ersthelferausbildung (SST), CACES/Fahrerlaubnisse für Gabelstapler/Hubarbeitsbühnen; F-Gas-Kenntnisse im Umgang mit HLK-Dienstleistern.

 - Gültiger Führerschein.

Warum Sie bei uns arbeiten sollten!

Was The Exploration Company besonders macht und warum wir glauben, dass Sie gerne bei uns arbeiten werden:

postings.title: CAD & PLM Administration Intern
postings.description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building innovative aerospace technologies that advance the future of space transportation.

To support our growth, we are looking for a CAD & PLM Administration Intern to join our team in Munich. In this hands-on role, you will help establish and maintain our CAD standard part library, provide first-level support to engineering users, and contribute to the documentation of CAD and PLM processes.




ROLE OVERVIEW

As a CAD & PLM Administration Intern, you will work closely with our engineering, CAD, PLM, and IT teams to help keep our design data and product lifecycle processes organised, accessible, and efficient.

Your primary focus will be supporting the creation and continuous improvement of a standard part library for CAD users. You will also act as a first point of contact for basic user requests and help create clear, practical documentation that enables our engineering teams to work effectively in a fast-paced aerospace environment.

This is an excellent opportunity to gain practical experience in CAD data management, PLM administration, engineering processes, and technical support while contributing to the development of a real space vehicle.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES




CAD AND PLM ADMINISTRATION

 - Support the creation, organisation, and maintenance of structured CAD and PLM data.

 - Support the setup and maintenance of CAD templates, standard part libraries, drafting standards, preferences, and other engineering environment settings.

 - Work with engineers and designers to identify opportunities to improve CAD workflows, data quality, reuse, and user experience.

 - Assist with testing and documenting changes to CAD and PLM processes, configurations, and system settings.

 - Gain hands-on experience with Siemens NX administration, including configuration concepts, customer defaults, role-based settings, templates, and environment configuration.

 - Learn about Siemens NX customization and automation possibilities under the guidance of experienced team members, for example through journals, reusable tools, interface settings, or workflow improvements.

 - Contribute to guidelines and best practices for CAD and PLM usage, including the appropriate use of standard parts and reusable engineering content.


DOCUMENTATION AND PROCESS SUPPORT

 - Create and maintain user guides, how-to instructions, process descriptions, and FAQs.

 - Document CAD and PLM procedures in a clear and accessible way.

 - Support the preparation of training material for new and existing users.


GENERAL CAD AND PLM ADMINISTRATION AND SUPPORT

 - Assist with routine administration and monitoring tasks in the CAD and PLM environment under supervision.

 - Support users and create documentation based on frequent support requests

 - Work with engineering, PLM, CAD, and IT colleagues to improve data quality and user experience.
   
   


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR




REQUIRED

 - Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's programme in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field.

 - Good communication skills in English.

 - Basic experience with Siemens NX and strong interest in CAD, engineering data management, PLM, or technical systems administration.

 - Organised, detail-oriented, and comfortable working with structured data and technical information.

 - A proactive, hands-on attitude and willingness to learn.

 - Comfortable working collaboratively in a multidisciplinary team.

postings.title: Control System Engineer
postings.description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building innovative aerospace technologies that advance the future of space transportation.



We are developing the control application for throttleable rocket engines. The team is responsible for designing, implementing, testing, and validating the closed-loop control and operational logic that allows the engine to operate safely and accurately across its operating envelope.


We are looking for a Control System and Model-Based Design Engineer to support both control algorithm development and application logic implementation. The role is suited for an intermediate engineer, or a strong junior, with good control fundamentals and practical experience developing control functions for real-world systems.


The objective is to help mature the engine control application, from early simulation and control design to MIL/SIL/HIL validation and analysis of real test data.



KEY RESPONSIBILITIES / TASKS


 - Design, tune, implement, and validate closed-loop control functions for fluidic systems, such as pressure, flow rate, pump speed, and valve position control.

 - Develop Simulink functions for control logic, sequencing, state machines, mode management, enable logic, limiters, protections, diagnostics, and actuator command generation.

 - Build and use control-oriented models, simulations, and test-data replay workflows to support design and validation.

 - Analyze controller performance, stability, robustness, actuator saturation, sensor limitations, delays, nonlinearities, and operating envelope constraints.

 - Implement practical control features such as PID, feedforward, filtering, gain scheduling, anti-windup, bumpless transfer, and mode-dependent control logic.

 - Support MIL, SIL, HIL, and test-data analysis activities to verify the behaviour of the control application before deployment.

 - Document design choices, assumptions, interfaces, validation results, limitations, and remaining risks.

 - Work closely with propulsion, embedded software, electronics, test, modelling, and systems engineering teams.

 - Practical experience developing functions in MATLAB/Simulink.

 - Experience implementing and testing control or embedded application logic for a real physical system.

 - Ability to analyze logs, simulation results, and test data to understand system behaviour and improve the design.

postings.title: EMC/EMI Engineer
postings.description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building innovative aerospace technologies that advance the future of space transportation.



We are seeking an experienced and motivated EMC/EMI Engineer to join our team. The successful candidate will be responsible for developing design recommendations and establishing test policies related to Electromagnetic Compatibility (EMC) and Electromagnetic Interference (EMI) for our spacecraft applications. This role requires a thorough understanding of EMC/EMI principles, spacecraft systems, and industry standards to ensure the reliability and functionality of our spacecraft in harsh space environments.



Key Responsibilities:



 1. Design and Development:
    
    - Provide expert guidance on EMC/EMI design practices to ensure spacecraft systems meet all relevant standards and requirements.
    
    - Collaborate with cross-functional teams to integrate EMC/EMI considerations into the design phase of spacecraft systems and subsystems.
    
    - Review and analyze design documents, schematics, and layout plans to identify potential EMC/EMI issues.



 1. Testing and Validation:
    
    - Develop and implement comprehensive EMC/EMI test plans and procedures for spacecraft systems.
    
    - Conduct EMC/EMI testing, including pre-compliance and compliance testing.
    
    - Analyze test data, identify non-conformities, and recommend corrective actions to resolve EMC/EMI issues.



 1. Standards and technological watch:
    
    - Ensure all designs and test procedures comply with relevant EMC/EMI standards
    
    - Stay updated with the latest developments in EMC/EMI standards and incorporate them into design and testing processes.



 1. Documentation and Reporting:
    
    - Prepare detailed technical reports, test summaries, and design documentation related to EMC/EMI activities.
    
    - Maintain accurate records of all test results, design recommendations, and corrective actions.



 1. Collaboration and Support:
    
    - Work closely with system engineers, hardware designers, and other stakeholders to address EMC/EMI challenges throughout the product development lifecycle.
    
    - Provide technical support and training to engineering teams on EMC/EMI best practices and mitigation techniques.



Qualifications:

 - Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, or a related field.

 - Minimum of 5 years of experience in EMC/EMI engineering, preferably in the aerospace or defense industry.

 - Strong knowledge of EMC/EMI principles, test methods, and mitigation techniques.

 - Experience with EMC/EMI standards, such as MIL-STD-461, CISPR, and DO-160.

 - Proficiency in using EMC/EMI testing equipment, including spectrum analyzers, network analyzers, and EMI receivers.

 - Excellent problem-solving skills and attention to detail.

 - Strong communication and interpersonal skills, with the ability to work effectively in a team environment.

 - Ability to manage multiple projects and priorities in a fast-paced environment.



Preferred Qualifications:

postings.description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building innovative aerospace technologies that advance the future of space transportation.

You will own the functional architecture and performance of the propellant feed system for a storable bipropellant propulsion system (MON3-MMH system). You will be responsible for ensuring the feed system delivers propellants to the thrusters within required specifications across the full mission envelope — from ground fill through operation, and recovery.




ROLE OVERVIEW

System Architecture

System Development

 - Identify key verification and validation steps required at the system and subsystem level to demonstrate compliance with specification

Modeling & Analysis

 - Develop and maintain fluid system models (steady-state and transient) to predict pressure drop, flow rates, water hammer, thruster cross-coupling, and priming behavior.

 - Verify compliance between system nominal and off-nominal operation with subsystem operational domains (such as thruster envelope).

 - Analyze failure modes (leakage, contamination, cavitation, fluid hammer) and define mitigation strategies and design margins.

Verification & Test

 - Lead functional and performance verification: cold-flow, functional and hot-fire tests from component to assembly level .

 - Correlate test data against predictive models and update margins/requirements accordingly.

 Integration Support

postings.title: In-Orbit Services Fault Management Engineer
postings.description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building innovative aerospace technologies that advance the future of space transportation.



Our In-Orbit Services unit is dedicated to expanding and complementing these capabilities by conceptualizing and developing new technologies, products and programs.



We are seeking a methodical Fault Management Engineer to help us strike the right balance between performance and reliability. The In-Orbit Services Fault Management Engineer is responsible for ensuring the reliability, availability, maintainability, and safety of orbital service vehicles and systems. This role is central to the design, development, and operational assurance of in-orbit service missions, supporting both technical risk reduction and mission success.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES



 - Fault Management Strategy:
   
   - Define, implement and validate fault management strategies, including Failure Detection, Isolation, and Recovery (FDIR) logic for in-orbit service vehicles.
   
   - Coordinate between hardware and flight software teams to architect robust and lean fault management solutions.



 - RAMS Analyses & Assurance:
   
   - Lead the definition and execution of fault tree analyses (FTA) and Failure Modes, Effects, and Criticality Analyses (FMECA) to identify and mitigate potential failure modes.
   
   - Perform reliability and availability prediction studies and allocate reliability targets to subsystems and equipment.
   
   - Conduct hazard analyses for ground, orbital, and re-entry phases, ensuring compliance with relevant safety requirements, including the safety analysis for launch authorities.



 - Continuous Improvement:
   
   - Collect and analyze in-orbit data to inform lessons learned and drive improvements in fault management and overall system reliability.
   
   - Support the creation and improvement of RAMS analysis tools and technical documentation.



 - Collaboration & Communication:
   
   - Work closely with multidisciplinary engineering teams (mechanical, thermal, avionics, software, operations, systems) to integrate RAMS and fault management requirements throughout the project lifecycle.
   
   - Prepare and present technical data, recommendations, and reports to internal and external stakeholders.




WHAT WE WOULD LOVE TO SEE FROM YOU

In the role of In-Orbit Services Fault Management Engineer, ideally you will have the following:



 - Education: Advanced degree (Master’s or PhD) in engineering, aerospace, or a related field; specialization in electronics, system engineering or fault management is a plus.

 - Technical skills: Proficiency in reliability tools (FMECA, FTA, reliability block diagrams) and fault management methodologies.

 - Experience: Hands-on experience with spacecraft FDIR strategy definition and validation planning and execution.

 - Communication: Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to convey technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders.

 - Feedback: Willingness to give proactive and mindful feedback across all company levels.

The Lead Flight Software owns the end-to-end delivery of all flight software, simulation environments, and supporting tools and software test setups required to fly, verify, and certify the vehicle.

This is a hands-on leadership role. You will manage four teams (~20 engineers total) while staying technically sharp and deeply involved in architecture, trade-offs, and critical design decisions. You are accountable for delivering reliable, certifiable software in a fast-moving, resource-constrained startup environment.




WHAT YOU WILL DO

You will define and evolve the overall flight software architecture, ensuring that it is robust, scalable, and aligned with mission and safety requirements. You will personally drive key architectural and system-level decisions, review critical designs and code, and ensure that technical trade-offs are made deliberately and transparently.

You will establish a strong interface between flight software, avionics, GNC, systems engineering, and safety teams, making sure that integration risks are identified early and resolved systematically. You will shape the verification and validation ecosystem, including SIL, HIL, and Monte Carlo campaigns, and automated test pipelines. It will be your responsibility to ensure that simulation and testing are not afterthoughts but central pillars of the program.

You will align software development plans with overall program milestones and vehicle integration timelines. You will represent flight software in major program reviews and external technical exchanges, including certification discussions with NASA and other stakeholders, and you will ensure a professional and well-prepared interface with IV&V organizations.

At the same time, you will build and lead a high-performing organization. You will coach team leads, grow senior engineers, establish engineering standards, and create a culture of ownership and accountability. You will set expectations clearly, make hard calls when needed, and ensure that the team delivers, all while prioritizing working software over paperwork without losing track of certification goals.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

In your capacity as a Lead Flight Software, your role will be continuously evolving, but day to day your duties will include:

 - Lead the design, development, and testing of the flight software for the spacecraft and all related elements

 - Manage and oversee the software development team to ensure timely delivery of high-quality software

 - Collaborate with other teams and departments, such as avionics, GNC, and systems, to ensure seamless integration of the software with other systems

 - Develop and implement software development processes and best practices to ensure efficient and effective development

 - Ensure the software meets all safety, performance, and reliability requirements

 - Continuously evaluate and improve the software to meet changing mission needs and incorporate new technologies

 - Stay up-to-date with the latest advancements in software development for spacecraft and related systems.

 - Get your hands-dirty by contributing to the flight software code and tests

 - Promote and develop the skills and capabilities of your team members and support their development




WHAT WE WOULD LOVE TO SEE FROM YOU

In the role of Lead Flight Software ideally, you will have the following:

 - Extensive experience in designing, developing, and testing flight software for spacecrafts or related systems

 - Strong leadership and management skills to lead a software development team and ensure timely delivery of high-quality software

 - Excellent collaboration skills to work effectively with other teams and departments, such as avionics and systems, to ensure seamless integration of the software with other systems

 - Knowledge and experience in implementing software development processes and best practices to ensure efficient and effective development

 - Ability to ensure the software meets all safety, performance, and reliability requirements and continuously evaluate and improve the software to meet changing mission needs and incorporate new technologies

 - Up-to-date knowledge of the latest advancements in software development for spacecraft and related systems

 - Hands-on coding and testing skills to contribute to the flight software code and tests with C/C++

 - Ability to promote and develop the skills and capabilities of team members and support their development.

Why you should join us!

What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is:  

 - We’re Agile - we make decisions fast whilst keeping our goals and systems in mind

postings.title: Lead Mission Assurance Engineer
postings.description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building innovative aerospace technologies that advance the future of space transportation.

We are looking for a Lead Mission Assurance Engineer to lead our Mission Assurance team and own the end-to-end strategy that ensures our spacecraft is safe, reliable, and mission ready. In this role you will be embedded with the design, test, and operations teams, driving the vehicle safety architecture as well as relentlessly driving risk down and availability up. In this role you will be the technical authority for mission assurance across the program and get to lead and mentor a team of ~6 mission assurance engineers.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

 - End-to-end ownership of the vehicle safety architecture making sure it meets all safety & reliability requirements (both internal and external from ISS program, ESA and CNES on entry safety).

 - Owner of overall flight reliability, responsible for assessing pre-flight risks and potential mitigations with vehicle design, analysis, and operations teams.

 - Perform and review FMECA, FTA, PRA, and RAM analyses to identify risks and failure modes.

 - Define and validate the spacecraft fault management and FDIR architecture.

 - Work with avionics, software, and operations teams to implement fault management strategies and ensure safe behavior under off-nominal conditions.

 - Support on-console operations as the Mission Assurance representative and drive in-flight anomaly resolution. Ensure lessons learned feed directly back into design and FDIR improvements.

 - Lead and mentor a team of safety, reliability, and fault management engineers. Set priorities, review their work, and grow their technical depth.

 - Champion a culture of mission assurance. Instill first-principles thinking, disciplined verification, and data-driven decision-making.

 - Report to program leadership on RAMS status, residual risk, and flight readiness.

 - Drive corrective actions from anomalies, test failures, and operational events back into design improvements.




WHAT WE WOULD LOVE TO SEE FROM YOU

The ideal candidate will have:

 - Master’s degree in an engineering or science discipline.

 - 8+ years of experience in RAMS, mission assurance, or systems safety on complex hardware systems.

 - Experience leading teams or projects — setting technical direction and delivering results.

 - Proficiency with reliability tools (e.g., FMECA, FTA, reliability block diagrams).

 - Deep understanding of fault tolerance, redundancy management, and failure detection/isolation/recovery.

 - Technical knowledge of spacecraft systems and operations (e.g., communications, orbital mechanics, avionics, propulsion, thermal control, life support systems).

 - Strong written and verbal communication of technical information.

 - Able to effectively manage projects and tasks while meeting aggressive deadlines.

 - Thrives under pressure and is resilient in the face of technical challenges.

 - Excellent organizational and interpersonal skills.




BONUS QUALIFICATIONS

 - Experience developing and validating FDIR logic, watchdog strategies, and fault response sequences.

 - Previous experience in a customer-facing role working through design requirements, test acceptance, and verification (especially with a government customer such as ESA/NASA).

 - Ability and willingness to put in extra time to mentor other engineers while also being a significant individual contributor.

 - Passion for advancing the commercial space industry and human spaceflight.

Why you should join us!

 - We’re Agile - we make decisions fast whilst keeping our goals and systems in mind 

 - We’re Open and Collaborative - we are transparent about risks and obstacles, so that we can cooperate to overcome them

Building on this heritage, our Future Projects activities are developing new orbital services and spacecraft applications for institutional, commercial and defence customers. This is a high-impact role for an experienced spacecraft project manager who can translate customer needs into executable programmes and lead multidisciplinary teams from early concept and proposal phases through design, qualification, launch, commissioning and operations. postings.title: Lunar Lander Test Bench Development Senior Engineer
postings.description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building innovative aerospace technologies that advance the future of space transportation.



At The Exploration Company, we are developing next-generation space transportation systems, including a lunar lander capable of precision landing and reusable operations. To support this effort, we are establishing a dedicated remote test site in the United Arab Emirates to perform hot-fire propulsion testing and hopper flight demonstrations.



As a Lunar Lander Test Bench Development Engineer, you will lead the design, development, and deployment of this new test facility from concept to operations. The role combines propulsion test infrastructure design, cryogenic fluid systems engineering, civil infrastructure coordination, and end-to-end project execution in a remote environment.



This position requires periodic travel to the UAE during site development, commissioning, and operations phases.

 


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES / TASKS

In this role, your responsibilities will evolve with project maturity. Day-to-day duties will include:



Test Site Development

 - Define and synthesize system-level requirements for a remote lunar lander test site supporting hot firing and hopper flight testing.

 - Lead the design and implementation of the complete facility, including ground infrastructure and utilities.

 - Specify and implement propellant and pressurization systems including Liquid Oxygen, Liquid Methane, Helium, and Nitrogen.

 - Design infrastructure enabling autonomous operation of a remote site (power generation, storage, logistics, safety systems).



Fluid and Cryogenic Systems Engineering

 - Develop P&IDs for propulsion test facilities and associated ground support equipment.

 - Design, size, and select components for cryogenic and high-pressure fluid systems.

 - Ensure safe handling, storage, and distribution of cryogenic propellants and pressurants.



Infrastructure and Civil Engineering Coordination

 - Define facility layout, foundations, structural interfaces, and site infrastructure requirements.

 - Coordinate with civil engineering partners to implement test stands, safety perimeters, and support buildings.

Safety, Automation, and Operations

 - Define and implement automation architectures for test operations and facility control, including safe connections with the vehicle to test.

 - Develop and validate safety-critical systems protecting personnel, hardware, and environment.

 - Perform hazard analyses (FMEA, HAZOP, risk assessments) and implement mitigation measures.

 - Develop test procedures, operational concepts, and commissioning plans.



Project Leadership

 - Lead end-to-end development of the test facility including design, procurement, manufacturing, installation, commissioning, and operations readiness.

 - Manage technical interfaces with internal teams, customers, and external suppliers.

 - Perform trade-off analyses to optimize performance, safety, cost, and schedule.

 - Support on-site deployment, integration, and test campaigns in the UAE.

 


WHAT WE WOULD LOVE TO SEE FROM YOU

 - Degree in aerospace engineering, mechanical engineering, energy systems, or a related field.

 - 5+ years of experience in propulsion test facilities or hot-fire test bench development.

 - Strong expertise in fluid systems engineering, including cryogenic propellants.

 - Experience designing or operating ground support equipment for rocket propulsion systems.

 - Knowledge of automation systems and safety-critical control architectures for industrial or test environments.

 - Experience coordinating infrastructure or facility development in industrial or remote environments.

 - Demonstrated project management capability across multidisciplinary engineering activities.

 - Hands-on engineering mindset with strong problem-solving ability.

 - Excellent communication skills and ability to work across international teams.

As a Lunar Lander Test Bench Development Engineer, you will lead the design, development, and deployment of this new test facility from concept to operations. The role combines propulsion test infrastructure design, cryogenic fluid systems engineering, civil infrastructure coordination, and end-to-end project execution in a remote environment.

 

This position requires periodic travel to the UAE during site development, commissioning, and operations phases.

 


KEY RESPONSIBILITIES / TASKS

Test Site Development

 - Lead the design and implementation of the complete facility, including ground infrastructure and utilities.

 - Specify and implement propellant and pressurization systems including Liquid Oxygen, Liquid Methane, Helium, and Nitrogen.

Fluid and Cryogenic Systems Engineering

 - Develop P&IDs for propulsion test facilities and associated ground support equipment.

 - Design, size, and select components for cryogenic and high-pressure fluid systems.

Infrastructure and Civil Engineering Coordination

 - Coordinate with civil engineering partners to implement test stands, safety perimeters, and support buildings.

Safety, Automation, and Operations

 - Define and implement automation architectures for test operations and facility control, including safe connections with the vehicle to test.

 - Develop and validate safety-critical systems protecting personnel, hardware, and environment.

 - Perform hazard analyses (FMEA, HAZOP, risk assessments) and implement mitigation measures.

 - Develop test procedures, operational concepts, and commissioning plans.

 

Project Leadership

 - Lead end-to-end development of the test facility including design, procurement, manufacturing, installation, commissioning, and operations readiness.

 - Manage technical interfaces with internal teams, customers, and external suppliers.

 - Perform trade-off analyses to optimize performance, safety, cost, and schedule.

 - Support on-site deployment, integration, and test campaigns.

 


WHAT WE WOULD LOVE TO SEE FROM YOU

postings.title: Principal Advanced Machining Engineer
postings.description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building innovative aerospace technologies that advance the future of space transportation.


[FRENCH VERSION BELOW/VERSION FRANÇAISE CI-DESSOUS]

ABOUT THE ROLE

The Exploration Company is looking for a Principal Advanced Machining Engineer to lead and structure our CNC machining workshop in Bordeaux.

Join The Exploration Company as a Principal Advanced Machining Engineer and act as the key link between Design teams, CAM/CNC programming and shop-floor execution for complex space hardware.

Based at our Bordeaux–Le Haillan site, you will provide technical leadership to a CNC team of around six people, with additional resources depending on workload. You will support Nyx and future space programs through a combination of manufacturing engineering, Design for Manufacturing and operational workshop management.

Your role will be to transform design intent into robust and efficient manufacturing solutions, while ensuring that the team, processes and machine park perform effectively every day.

The workshop covers 3-axis and 5-axis milling, CNC turning, mill-turn, grinding and Wire EDM activities. You will report to the Lead Advanced Manufacturing.



WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Lead, support and develop the CNC workshop team.

 - Organise daily priorities, workload, machine allocation and production follow-up.

 - Drive shop-floor routines covering progress, blockers, safety, quality and delivery risks.

 - Act as the main interface between Design, Manufacturing Engineering, CNC programmers and machinists.

 - Contribute early to Design for Manufacturing activities, including manufacturability, tolerances, datums, tool access, workholding, machining sequences and inspection strategy.

 - Support and challenge CNC programming, machining strategies, setups, tooling and workholding.

 - Coordinate machining activities across milling, turning, mill-turn, grinding and Wire EDM.

 - Manage the capability, availability and performance of the CNC machine park, including first-level maintenance and preventive maintenance follow-up.

 - Improve workshop performance through machine utilisation, setup time, first-time-right, rework reduction and delivery adherence.

 - Manage team skills development, training, onboarding and technical standards.

 - Support equipment investments, capacity planning, supplier selection and machine commissioning.

 - Coordinate with Design, MAIT, Quality, Metrology, Production and Supply Chain.

 - Ensure appropriate production control, traceability, documentation and non-conformity management.


WHAT YOU BRING

 - An engineering degree in mechanical, manufacturing, industrialisation or machining engineering.

 - Significant experience in manufacturing engineering, industrialisation or advanced CNC machining, including CAM and HyperMill.

 - Strong knowledge of Design for Manufacturing, GD&T, functional tolerancing and machining processes.

 - Experience leading a technical team and managing workshop priorities, capacity and machine-park performance.

 - Experience in aerospace, space or another high-precision industrial environment.

 - Professional proficiency in English and French.


WHY JOIN US

 - Lead and develop a strategic CNC workshop for a European space company.

 - Work on critical hardware for Nyx and future space programs.

 - Combine upstream manufacturing engineering with real responsibility for people, processes and equipment.

 - Have a direct impact on Design for Manufacturing, industrial maturity and workshop performance.


/////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////////




À PROPOS DU POSTE

The Exploration Company recherche un(e) Principal Advanced Machining Engineer pour diriger et structurer notre atelier d'usinage CNC à Bordeaux.

Rejoignez The Exploration Company en tant que Principal Advanced Machining Engineer et devenez le lien clé entre les équipes de conception, la programmation CAM/CNC et l'exécution en atelier pour des équipements spatiaux complexes.

Basé(e) sur notre site de Bordeaux–Le Haillan, vous apporterez un leadership technique à une équipe CNC d'environ six personnes, avec des ressources additionnelles selon la charge de travail. Vous soutiendrez le programme Nyx ainsi que les futurs programmes spatiaux, en combinant ingénierie de fabrication, conception pour la fabrication (Design for Manufacturing) et gestion opérationnelle de l'atelier.

Votre rôle sera de transformer les intentions de conception en solutions de fabrication robustes et efficaces, tout en veillant à ce que l'équipe, les processus et le parc machines fonctionnent efficacement au quotidien.

L'atelier couvre les activités de fraisage 3 et 5 axes, tournage CNC, tournage-fraisage (mill-turn), rectification et découpe par électroérosion à fil (Wire EDM). Vous serez rattaché(e) au Lead Advanced Manufacturing.



VOS MISSIONS

 - Diriger, accompagner et développer l'équipe de l'atelier CNC.

 - Organiser les priorités quotidiennes, la charge de travail, l'allocation des machines et le suivi de production.

 - Animer les routines d'atelier couvrant l'avancement, les blocages, la sécurité, la qualité et les risques de livraison.

This role is integral to the Software team, ensuring that our software products meet the highest standards of reliability, performance, and compliance with contractual requirements.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES



As a Software Product Assurance (SW PA) Engineer, you will hold a crucial position within the Software Team. You will serve as the SW quality focal point for space projects, with a primary focus on the Nyx Earth project. Your duties will encompass a wide range of responsibilities, including but not limited to:



 - Establishing and maintaining the project's SW PA&S requirements baseline in compliance with applicable NASA/ESA requirements and best market practices.

 - Supporting Independent Verification and Validation (IV&V) activities, working in coordination with IV&V personnel to mitigate software risks and enhance safety and quality.

 - Managing SW nonconformities, deviations, alerts, and assessing their impact.

 - Contributing to the risk management process and managing SW Critical Items.

 - Managing and applying SW lessons learned.

 - Planning, conducting and following up on project SW audits.

 - Overseeing configuration management processes to ensure alignment with approved plans, including identification, status accounting, change control, verification, and delivery.

 - Ensuring software reliability and maintainability requirements are met and traceable to system requirements.

WHAT WE WOULD LOVE TO SEE FROM YOU

In the role of SW Product Assurance Engineer ideally, you will have the following:

 - A bachelor in engineering or technical sciences

postings.title: Spacecraft Flight Computing Senior Engineer
postings.description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building innovative aerospace technologies that advance the future of space transportation.



The Exploration Company is seeking a highly skilled Spacecraft Flight Computing Engineer with expertise in real-time, fault-tolerant computer systems running a RTOS and/or Linux. This role is focused on hands-on hardware and software development, with an emphasis on building systems resilient to radiation effects in space environments. The engineer will also apply knowledge of IP networking, including Time-Sensitive Networking (TSN) and Precision Time Protocol (PTP), to enable deterministic, synchronized communication across spacecraft subsystems.



Key Responsibilities



 - Design, implement, and maintain real-time embedded computing systems for spacecraft avionics.

 - Apply fault-tolerant computing techniques to ensure reliable operation in the presence of radiation-induced upsets and anomalies.

 - Develop and optimize our RTOS and Linux-based real-time operating environments, including kernel configuration, bootloader, device drivers, and system-level performance tuning.

 - Perform hardware design tasks, including schematic capture, PCB layout, and component selection using Altium Designer, with emphasis on radiation-tolerant design practices.

 - Develop, synthesize, and validate FPGA designs (VHDL/Verilog), incorporating mitigation strategies such as TMR, ECC, and scrubbing.

 - Design, configure, and troubleshoot IP networking protocols, with focus on TSN for deterministic networking and PTP for precise time synchronization across spacecraft systems.

 - Conduct system integration, hardware/software debugging, and fault injection testing to verify robustness under radiation and fault conditions.

 - Collaborate closely with flight software, avionics, and systems engineering teams to define computing, networking, and interface requirements.

 - Support mission operations through anomaly resolution and post-flight analysis of radiation-induced effects such as SEUs and TID.



Required Qualifications



 - Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Computer Science, or a related field.

 - Strong proficiency in C/C++ and Python for embedded software development and automation.

 - Hands-on experience with real-time systems and Linux-based embedded computing.

 - Practical expertise in fault-tolerant computing methods (redundancy, checkpoint/restart, graceful degradation).

 - Knowledge of IP networking protocols (TCP/IP, UDP, routing, switching) with direct experience implementing TSN and PTP in real-time or mission-critical environments.

 - Understanding of radiation effects on electronics and software, with experience implementing mitigation strategies at multiple system levels.

 - Experience with system-level debugging tools and hardware/software integration.



What we would love to see from you



 - Strong skills in writing, debugging and performance tuning low-level software for Linux and/or a RTOS, including the bootloader and device drivers.

 - Strong skills in hardware design using Altium Designer and/or Cadence Allegro for schematics and PCB layout. Bonus points if you have experience with multi-gigabit SERDES interfaces like SGMII, PCI Express and Serial RapidIO.

 - Solid background in FPGA development (VHDL/Verilog, synthesis, simulation, timing closure, hardware validation).

 - Familiarity with modern multi-core ARM-based System-on-Chip hardware, including the internal architecture.

 - Experience writing bare-metal code.

 - Strong skills in writing low-level software for Linux and/or a RTOS, including the bootloader and device drivers.

 - Exposure to radiation testing (heavy-ion, proton, or TID) and analysis.

 - Background in hardware-software co-design for reliability and fault-tolerance.

 - Prior hands-on experience supporting space missions.



What's special about TEC's Flight Computing team?



Our team is led by some the very best minds in the aerospace industry. We are experts in fault-tolerant spacecraft avionics and we’ve played significant roles within NASA/JPL’s avionics and robotics communities, SpaceX, Virgin Orbit and Google.

We’ve designed hardware and software for use on Earth, the International Space Station, in orbit around Earth's moon, Mars, Saturn and Jupiter. As a hardcore engineering team, we don’t believe in half measures and we’re looking for more engineers just like us. If this sounds like where you belong, I’d like to hear from you.

 - Direct involvement in building mission-critical spacecraft systems that operate in extreme environments.

 - A collaborative engineering culture where hands-on innovation, resilience, and reliability drive success.

 - Competitive compensation, comprehensive benefits, and opportunities for technical growth.



Due to federal regulations (e.g., ITAR/EAR), applicants must be U.S. citizens or lawful permanent residents (green card holders).

You will own spacecraft-level thermal test campaigns, including Thermal Vacuum (TVAC) and Thermal Balance testing, support AIT with the Thermal Control System Flight Model integration and verification, coordinate thermal qualification activities with other sub-systems, and ensure compliance with spacecraft verification requirements.

 - Prepare and lead Test Readiness Reviews, Test Review Board and NCR Board

postings.title: Storm test bench program manager
postings.description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building innovative aerospace technologies that advance the future of space transportation.



Storm is TEC’s high-performance liquid rocket engine program, developed to support next-generation launch and space transportation applications. The Storm development strategy relies heavily on ground testing, from early development models to qualification and acceptance campaigns. The engine test bench is a critical enabler of the program, and its on-time delivery is essential to maintain the Storm development schedule.



As Storm Engine Test Bench Program Manager, you are responsible for driving the on-time delivery of the Storm engine test bench development program. You will ensure execution discipline across the bench development workstream: integrating schedules, tracking deliverables, coordinating stakeholders and suppliers, anticipating blockers, and escalating decisions to keep the program on track. In addition, you will act as the primary point of contact for identifying and securing a suitable test bench location, coordinating the site selection process with internal stakeholders and external parties.



KEY RESPONSIBILITIES




PROGRAM PLANNING AND DELIVERY (SCHEDULE, SCOPE, COST TRACKING)

 - Build, maintain, and continuously improve the integrated test bench delivery plan (design maturity gates, procurement lead times, manufacturing, installation, integration, and commissioning support activities).

 - Own the critical path, dependencies, and milestone readiness criteria (from a delivery perspective).

 - Track progress, identify schedule threats early, and drive recovery plans (re-sequencing, parallelization, expediting, resourcing proposals).

 - Maintain program routines (weekly reviews, action tracking, decision logs) to ensure execution discipline.


CROSS-FUNCTIONAL COORDINATION AND COMMUNICATION

 - Animate weekly/monthly routines: bench program reviews, schedule reviews, and interface meetings

 - Ensure alignment between propulsion engineering, test engineering, facilities/infrastructure, procurement, quality, and site teams

 - Prepare concise reporting for program leadership: status, risks, mitigation, upcoming decisions, and milestone readiness

 - Coordinate preparation of key internal reviews (bench concept reviews, design/package readiness, delivery readiness checkpoints)


TEST BENCH LOCATION IDENTIFICATION AND SITE SELECTION (POINT OF CONTACT)

 - Act as the single point of contact to identify, assess, and secure a test bench location aligned with the Storm schedule and development needs.

 - Coordinate the site selection process (timeline, stakeholder alignment, decision gates, and documentation) and ensure decisions are taken in time to protect the critical path.

 - With support from the engineering team (who define requirements and technical needs), consolidate the test site needs impacting the choice of location and translate them into:
   
   - A practical location assessment checklist (capabilities, utilities, access, constraints)
   
   - A comparison of candidate sites (schedule, cost, readiness, risks)
   
   - Clear decision packages for leadership (trade-offs, recommended option, fallback plans)

 - Coordinate interfaces with external stakeholders as needed (site operators, landlords/partners, utilities, local service providers), in alignment with internal owners.


PROCUREMENT AND SUPPLIER COORDINATION

 - Coordinate long-lead procurement tracking

 - Support supplier selection and onboarding (RFI/RFQ process coordination, delivery tracking, expediting)

 - Monitor supplier performance and ensure timely resolution of delivery issues, NCR handling coordination, and logistics readiness

 - Ensure documentation deliverables from suppliers are collected and integrated


INTEGRATION AND COMMISSIONING READINESS SUPPORT

 - Ensure prerequisites for integration/commissioning are planned and tracked: procedures availability, resources, tooling, spares, training needs and documentation readiness (owned by responsible teams)

 - Track open points, coordinate closure plans, and ensure readiness evidence is available for management decisions.

 - Support lessons-learned capture and incorporation into the next iterations of bench capability


WHAT WE WOULD LIKE TO SEE FROM YOU

 - Master’s degree (or equivalent) in Aerospace Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Systems Engineering, or similar

 - Significant experience delivering complex test infrastructure or propulsion tests programs

 - Proven program management experience (planning, budgeting, risk, suppliers)

 - Strong understanding of propulsion testing, cryogenic systems, and hazardous operations

 - Experience with LOX/methane engine testing or cryogenic facilities

 - Familiarity with European space programs and standards (e.g. ECSS, ESA‑style reviews)

 - Experience with regulated industrial sites, permitting, or environmental compliance

 - Background in high‑cadence test operations

 - Ability to lead cross‑functional teams and make sound technical and operational decisions

 - Strong ownership and delivery mindset

 - Systems‑level thinking and interface management

 - Calm decision‑making during high‑pressure test activities

 - Strong documentation and reporting discipline

 - Fluent in English; French or German is a plus.



Why you should join us!

What makes us special here at The Exploration Company and why we think you will enjoy working here is:

postings.description:

We want you as a talented Supply Chain Manufacturing Engineer (Metals) to help us in our mission by supporting the design team to build up the Nyx vehicle. As process engineer you will:

 - Work together with the mechanical and design units to support through our supply chain the manufacturing of complex metallic structures,

 - You will work closely with the product assurance and procurement team to help controlling the quality of the final delivered products.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

You will have a key responsibility at the technical crossroad between vehicle design team, product assurance team and procurement team. Your role will be continuously evolving, but day to day your duties will include:

 - Taking responsibility for technical exchanges with suppliers about manufacturing of metallic structural parts. Under the intended product owner guidance you act as a technical liaison between the company and its suppliers, facilitating clear and open communication to address any manufacturing related issue promptly.

 - Monitoring suppliers industrial process, and if necessary propose improvements, to make sure the final product meets the requirements.

 - Supervising supplier's development roadmaps from TRL 4-5 up to TRL 9, assuring the proper technology development.

 - Partnering with the Product Assurance team to monitor supplier quality control plans, required standards, specifically focusing on NDT (Non-Destructive Testing) and material certifications.

 - Collaborating continuously with engineering team and suppliers to accomplish the delivery of final products, from engineering models up to final flight models, in accordance with schedule.

 - Supporting suppliers to analyse and improve their industrial processes, considering challenges of large-scale machining, sheet metal bending, additive manufacturing, and specialized joining (e.g. welded structures).

 - Documentation for the various reviews (TRL review, PDR, CDR, QR, MRR)

 - Deep knowledge of high-performance alloys (Aluminium, Titanium, Inconel) and manufacturing methods such as 5-axis machining, sheet metal bending, coating, heat treatment, ALM (Additive Layer Manufacturing), and forging.

ROLE OVERVIEW



FLUID SYSTEM DESIGN & FUNCTIONAL ANALYSIS

 - Mature the overall fluid system from detailed design to qualification by leading the functional analysis of the assembly

 - Lead your own analysis tasks using advanced simulation tools, and provide outputs to other fluid analysts and functional engineers in selecting appropriate methodologies, assumptions, and data processing methods.

System Architecture & Trade Studies

 - Support development and qualification ground platform designs

 - Contribute to ground platforms and flight simulations, sensitivity analyses, and risk assessments.

 - Plan and execute the V&V plan for the fluid subsystem, including analysis and test campaigns to verify subsystem performance and requirements compliance.

You will manage the team that develops, commissions and operates the test facility. This position requires technical excellence and expertise as well as team management skills.



KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Design of Test Facility

 - Develop a vacuum hot fire test facility which will be used to develop and qualify orbital thrusters

 - Capture and define system-level requirements for a chemical propulsion test bench supporting 100–800 N thrusters.

 - Define performance envelopes, safety objectives, operability constraints, and verification methods.

 - Translate propulsion test needs into facility, utilities, and ground support equipment requirements

 - Define instrumentation, data acquisition, and control systems for safe hot-fire testing.

 - Interface effectively with internal engineering/design teams, customers, and external partners.

Assembly & Integration of Test Facility

 - Define the schedule and conditions of the bench integration. Define the tests to be performed all along the project, to mitigate the risks to find issues during commissionning.

 - Manage suppliers and internal manufacturing activities; oversee integration and verification.

 - Plan and execute commissioning, acceptance testing, and entry-into-service activities.

Safety & Operation of Test Facility

 - Lead hazard analyses (FMEA, HAZOP, risk assessments) and implement mitigation measures.

 - Develop procedures for handling, testing, maintenance, and emergency response.

 - Validate redlines and abort sequences for different failure cases

 - Integration of thruster into test bench

 - Lead operations of test facility and perform hot fire, cold flows, decontamination and maintenance activities. It's possible that at one point, the operations would be handover to another testing team and then insure a smooth and well documented handover if needed.

Leadership / Team management

 - As a Team Leader we expect you to drive and support a small multidisciplinary team to design, procure, assemble, and install and commission the test bench.

 - You will manage the team tasks and priorities and partially HR/training and developpement topics



WHAT WE WOULD LOVE TO SEE FROM YOU

 - Strong background in fluid systems, pressurized systems, and ground support equipment.

postings.title: Valve Development Engineer
postings.description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building innovative aerospace technologies that advance the future of space transportation.


As a talented Valve Development Engineer, you will lead the design and development of solenoid isolation valves for our storable propulsion system, from concept through qualification — owning the electromagnetic, mechanical, and sealing design that makes the valve work reliably over the mission life.



ROLE OVERVIEW

Valve Design & Development

 - Support the design of solenoid isolation valves from concept through qualification, balancing performance, mass, reliability, and manufacturability.

 - Define and mature valve architecture — poppet/seat design, actuation mechanism, sealing concept — to meet functional and interface requirements.

 - Perform mechanical sizing and trade studies (force margins, spring rates, stroke, response time) to support design decisions.

Electromagnetic & Actuation Design

 - Design and analyze the solenoid actuator — coil, armature, magnetic circuit — to meet response time, power, and force margin requirements.

 - Collaborate with electrical engineers on coil drive electronics and EMI/EMC considerations.

 - Support trade-offs between actuation force, power consumption, and thermal dissipation.

Materials, Sealing & Propellant Compatibility

 - Select materials and seal designs compatible with storable propellants, ensuring long-term compatibility and low permeation/leakage.

 - Define sealing concepts — elastomeric or metal-to-metal — balancing leak-tightness, cycle life, and contamination sensitivity.

 - Coordinate with materials engineering on qualification of propellant-wetted materials.

Design Verification & Cross-Functional Coordination

 - Define and support the verification plan for valve qualification, working closely with test engineers on test setup and success criteria.

 - Collaborate with manufacturing engineers to ensure design manufacturability and testability.

 - Support anomaly investigations and root cause analysis for valve-level issues, feeding lessons learned back into the design.





KEY RESPONSIBILITIES


LOCATION

You will perform your duties principally at the Company's premises in Bordeaux and may be required to travel from time to time to our company’s premises in Munich in the course of your duties.


WHAT WE WOULD LOVE TO SEE FROM YOU

 - 5+ years of hands-on experience designing valves or similar electromechanical fluid components for space or aerospace applications.

 - Experience in solenoid/electromagnetic actuator design (magnetic circuit design, coil design) is a strong plus.

 - Strong understanding of sealing technology, elastomer and metal seal design, and propellant compatibility; storable propellant experience preferred.

 - Proficiency in CAD (CATIA, NX, or equivalent) and mechanical analysis tools.

 - Experience defining and supporting qualification test campaigns for valves.

 - Familiarity with applicable standards for valve qualification (NASA, ECSS, or equivalent).

postings.title: Wire Harness Technician (EWIS)
postings.description:
Here at The Exploration Company, we are building innovative aerospace technologies that advance the future of space transportation.



To support this mission, we are bringing harness manufacturing in-house and are looking for a Wire Harness Technician to help industrialize, build, and validate high-reliability electrical harnesses used across the Nyx avionics and test campaigns.

In this role, your scope will be continuously evolving. Day-to-day you will help translate harness design outputs into robust manufacturing processes and deliver flight-like and test harnesses with strong quality, repeatability, and documentation.




KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

In your capacity as a Wire Harness Technician, your responsibilities will typically include:



Manufacturing & Assembly Execution



 - Build electrical harnesses (development, qualification, and test harnesses), including cut/strip, crimp, splice, solder (where applicable), lacing/tie, over-braid/shield terminations, labeling, and final assembly.

 - Support batch-by-batch production for test campaigns and verification activities (e.g., shock/vibration, EMI/EMC, TVAC), coordinating readiness of parts, tooling, and work instructions.



Cross-functional Collaboration



 - Work closely with harness design and integration stakeholders to ensure manufacturability (DFM), clarity of drawings, and alignment between wiring diagrams and physical assembly.



Documentation & Traceability



 - Maintain “as-built” records, deviations, rework logs, and configuration/serial tracking for harnesses and critical components.




WHAT WE WOULD LOVE TO SEE FROM YOU



For the Wire Harness Technician role, you ideally bring experience with the following:

 - Technical vocational training (Ausbildung) in electrical, electronic, or mechanical fields (e.g. Elektroniker, Mechatroniker) or equivalent hands-on experience.

 - Strong hands-on experience with wiring harness manufacturing or cable assembly in high-reliability contexts (aerospace/space, aviation, motorsport, defense, medical, or similar).

 - Ability to interpret harness drawings, wiring diagrams, BOMs, and connector tables; comfortable working from controlled documentation and detailed work instructions.

 - Solid understanding of harness workmanship principles (crimp quality, strain relief, routing/bend radius, shielding/grounding practices, backshell assembly and torqueing, etc.).

 - Practical troubleshooting skills (identifying pinning errors, shorts/opens, intermittent faults, damaged contacts, shielding issues, etc.).

 - Experience using typical harness assembly tools (crimp tools, wire strippers, insertion/extraction tools, torque tools, soldering equipment when applicable).

 - High attention to detail and manual dexterity, with a strong focus on quality and workmanship standards (preferably IPC/WHMA awareness).

 - Ability to follow precise processes and work instructions while maintaining consistency and traceability during production.

 - Comfortable working in a fast-paced production or test environment where priorities can shift based on integration and delivery needs.

 - Team-oriented mindset with clear communication with engineering and quality teams when issues arise.




NICE TO HAVE



 - Familiarity with aerospace/space workmanship standards and inspection approaches (e.g., IPC-style workmanship, connector acceptance criteria, traceability practices).

 - Experience with harness electrical test equipment and automated test report generation.

 - Understanding of EMI/EMC-sensitive build practices (shield termination strategies, pigtail control, bonding/grounding considerations), aligned with the fact that harnesses support EMI/EMC test activities.

 - Prior experience supporting test harness builds for environmental testing (vibration, thermal-vac, etc.).
